His odds have also softened further after Vance publicly suggested he might not run, and he faces credible competition from figures like Marco Rubio for the nomination and Jon Ossoff on the Democratic side in a general election. This is highly consistent with the market's reference 'No' price of 83%, so I anchor close to but slightly below that based on the latest aggregated market data.

results.market_title: Will there be exactly 3 North Korea tests in October 2026?
results.reasoning: Web searches confirmed North Korea conducted qualifying missile tests on at least two separate calendar days in October 2026 (Oct 3 ballistic missile test, and Oct 11 twin submarine-launched missile test reported by KCNA/Al Jazeera around Oct 13-15). However, search tool access was cut off before I could confirm activity for the remainder of the month (Oct 16-31), leaving significant uncertainty about whether a third (or additional) qualifying test day occurred to make the total exactly 3 rather than 2, 4, or more. Given North Korea's historical pattern of frequent, clustered missile activity especially amid rising peninsula tensions (noted South Korean hypersonic missile test friction), a count landing exactly on 3 is plausible but far from certain.

executor.read: Venue: polymarket-us. Dry run while paperTradeMode is on: every paper entry/exit of the main lane is queued as an intent and consumed on the next 5-minute cron; each is routed to the Polymarket US moneyline (league -> game -> long/short side) and priced on that book with its 0.0695 x p(1-p) fee; clobRef is the same intent on the global CLOB for comparison. Nothing is placed while dry. order = the FOK limit the executor would send (YES-price convention, tick-rounded, contracts). execPriceC = volume-weighted effective price for the paper size; slippageC = cents worse than the paper price; wouldReject = live rules that would refuse it (min size, slippage cap 5c, thin book); wouldBlock = the daily risk gates. routing.unroutable = intents with no Polymarket US market (the live path skips those trades). roundTrips diff buy+sell (both fees) against the paper ledger; dryMinusPaper is how much paper overstates. Maker mode (orderMode): a BUY rests post-only at the best level on our side (good-till-date = the TTL) instead of crossing; dry fills it when the market trades through the level or a print lands there, and at the TTL takes the taker fill (fallback) or skips; takerRef on a maker fill is the FOK it would have sent at placement, so maker.savedVsTakerUsd and roundTrips.makerMinusTakerOnFilled are the maker edge on the trades that filled; maker.missed are entries that never filled. Exits stay taker. Live: only with paperTradeMode off and PMUS_KEY_ID/PMUS_SECRET_KEY set; consumes the live exec queue, FOK limit or close-position with synchronous execution, confirms fills to the auto-trader, reconciles ambiguous sends against the account position and halts itself if that fails. POST /autotrader/executor/halt is the kill switch.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator). crosses = those minutes listed (newest first, with the US shares shown on the side taken; Kalshi sizes are not sampled) and whether each was still there on the next row (persisted): the Kalshi read lands a few seconds before the US read inside a minute, so a cross gone a minute later is most likely a book catching up between the two reads; one game carrying most of a sport's crosses points at a mis-mapped Kalshi leg.

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1); exit fees and the US spread are not charged on those. marks.x5 / marks.x15 are the round trip: closed on the Polymarket US book 5 / 15 minutes later (the bid for a buy, the ask for a sell, so the spread is paid) with the exit taker fee charged too - what a scalping lane would actually have booked. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. marks.kh0 / marks.kh1 are the Kalshi hedge (Oct 30 2026): the same leg sold on Kalshi at its bid (for a buy) or bought at its ask (for a sell) as a taker, priced in the event minute (kh0) or at the next sample (kh1, the honest one: the US leg first, Kalshi a minute later); the US entry fee and Kalshi's taker fee are charged and the position is then locked whatever the game does, so this is what a two-venue, US-legal lane would book per share (Kalshi sizes are not sampled; usd uses the US shown size; noData = Kalshi not quoted there). kalshiQuoted = the events with a kh1 mark, so kh1 can be read against x5 / settle on the same events (all and tradable), with the games carrying most of them (one game holding a third or more is a stale-quote artefact, not a lane). Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, a Polymarket US lane is worth building only if the round trip (x5 or x15) is positive on the tradable subset with a hit rate above 50%, or settle is; a Kalshi-hedged lane only if kh1 is positive on the tradable subset at a hit rate above 50% over ~200 events with a Kalshi quote, and it beats x5; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.

scalp.read: The Polymarket US stale-quote scalp lane (src/scalp.js). Each minute the sampler sees global Polymarket's mid move 3c+ while the US quote has not followed and is still crossable after its taker fee, the lane takes the stale quote for up to $10 (never more than the shares shown) and closes on the US book 5 minutes later as a taker, both fees charged; pnlC is cents a share after both fees, the same number the paper lane's x5 mark reads. Modes: off / dry (decisions and fills at the sampled quotes, nothing sent) / live (FOK entry and close-position exit on Polymarket US with the account key; only when the key is on the worker). Risk: 3 open, 40 a day, stop at -$15 realized on the day, one scalp per game, edge >= 1c and 50+ shares shown; POST /xvenue/scalp/halt is the kill switch and the lane halts itself on an ambiguous send or an exit it cannot reconcile. exitKind: x5 = closed at the hold on a US quote; late_last_quote / no_quote = no US quote at the hold (dry), closed at the last quote seen or unpriced; x_live = the venue's close fill; settling = the venue refused the close (market over), the position settles there and its P&L lands in the account balance, not here. The live flip is the owner's.
